subject: general
question: Who was the Englishman who came to India, taught Philosophy in St Stephen’s College and later was known as ‘Deenbandhu’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**CF Andrews.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• C.F. Andrews arrived in India in **1904.**
 
• He began teaching at St. Stephen's College in **1911**.
 
• He became closely associated with** Mahatma Gandhi** in the 1910s and supported various movements until India gained independence in **1947**.
 
• Andrews earned the title** 'Deenbandhu'** (friend of the poor) for his commitment to social justice, focusing on the rights and welfare of the underprivileged.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **William Pitt:**

 
 
• William Pitt the Younger served as** Prime Minister of Great Britain** during the late 18th and early 19th centuries, playing a key role in the politics of the time.
 
• He was instrumental in passing the** India Act of 1784**, which aimed to reform the governance of British territories in India.
 
 
 
• **Lord Russell:**
 
 
• Lord John Russell was a British statesman and a prominent** Liberal Party leader**, serving twice as Prime Minister in the 19th century.
 
• He advocated for reforms in India, especially concerning governance and civil rights, but did not have a direct role in education like** C.F. Andrews**.
 
 
 
• **Michael Madhusudan Dutt:**
 
 
• Michael Madhusudan Dutt was a prominent **Bengali poet** and playwright known for his contributions to Bengali literature, particularly in the 19th century.
 
• He is credited with introducing the sonnet form to Bengali poetry and is often regarded as a precursor to modern **Bengali literature**.
